gaps.concept: Gestational age is counted from the last menstrual period, approximately two weeks before fertilization.
gaps.why_tested: A stem gives a conception date and asks for obstetric gestational age.

gaps.concept: Second-trimester ultrasound dating uses fetal head, abdominal circumference, and femur measurements; later scans are less accurate for dating.
gaps.why_tested: A patient presents without reliable menstrual dates after the first trimester.

gaps.concept: In first-trimester trisomy 21 screening, nuchal translucency and hCG increase while PAPP-A decreases.
gaps.why_tested: A stem supplies first-trimester markers and asks which aneuploidy is most likely.

gaps.concept: In first-trimester trisomy 18 screening, nuchal translucency increases while hCG and PAPP-A decrease.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks the learner to distinguish Edwards syndrome from Down syndrome using early screening results.

gaps.concept: Increased nuchal translucency also suggests Turner syndrome or a congenital heart defect, even with a normal chromosome screen.
gaps.why_tested: An abnormal ultrasound finding persists despite reassuring cell-free DNA results.

gaps.concept: Cell-free DNA is placental in origin and remains a screening test; a positive result requires CVS or amniocentesis for diagnosis.
gaps.why_tested: A patient asks whether a positive blood test establishes fetal aneuploidy.

gaps.concept: Confined placental mosaicism or a vanishing twin can cause discordant cell-free DNA results.
gaps.why_tested: A positive cell-free DNA screen conflicts with fetal diagnostic testing.

gaps.concept: Advanced maternal age increases baseline aneuploidy risk and the positive predictive value of screening.
gaps.why_tested: Identical positive screens are presented in patients of different ages.

gaps.concept: CVS samples placental tissue and cannot assess open neural tube defects; amniotic fluid AFP and acetylcholinesterase can.
gaps.why_tested: A patient needs diagnostic evaluation for an open neural tube defect.

gaps.concept: Closed neural tube defects may have normal maternal serum AFP; open defects leak AFP into amniotic fluid.
gaps.why_tested: A normal AFP result is contrasted with an ultrasound-detected spinal defect.

gaps.concept: Prenatal ultrasound may show lemon-shaped skull and banana-shaped cerebellum with open spina bifida and Chiari II malformation.
gaps.why_tested: A fetal ultrasound shows characteristic cranial signs of an open spinal defect.

gaps.concept: Gastroschisis has uncovered bowel beside the umbilicus; omphalocele is midline and membrane-covered, with stronger aneuploidy associations.
gaps.why_tested: Elevated AFP accompanies an abdominal wall defect on ultrasound.

gaps.concept: Prenatal carrier screening includes cystic fibrosis, spinal muscular atrophy, and hemoglobinopathies; testing an affected carrier’s partner assesses fetal risk.
gaps.why_tested: A healthy pregnant patient is found to carry an autosomal recessive variant.

gaps.concept: An Rh-negative, unsensitized pregnant patient receives anti-D immune globulin at approximately 28 weeks and after sensitizing events.
gaps.why_tested: Prenatal blood typing and antibody screening identify risk of fetal Rh alloimmunization.

gaps.concept: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy requires treatment because it increases maternal pyelonephritis risk.
gaps.why_tested: A routine urine culture is positive despite no urinary symptoms.

gaps.concept: Hepatitis B vaccination can be given during pregnancy when indicated; HPV vaccination is deferred until after pregnancy.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which vaccine can be administered to an unvaccinated pregnant patient.

gaps.concept: ACE inhibitors and ARBs can cause fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios, and skull hypoplasia, especially after the first trimester.
gaps.why_tested: A fetus develops oligohydramnios after maternal antihypertensive exposure.

gaps.concept: Warfarin embryopathy causes nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses; heparin does not cross the placenta.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnant patient needs anticoagulation, or a newborn has characteristic skeletal findings.

gaps.concept: Isotretinoin exposure causes craniofacial, cardiac, thymic, and central nervous system malformations.
gaps.why_tested: An acne medication exposure precedes multiple fetal anomalies.

gaps.concept: Valproate and carbamazepine increase neural tube defect risk; valproate is especially associated with spina bifida.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with epilepsy has a fetus with an open spinal defect.

gaps.concept: Fetal hydantoin syndrome from phenytoin features growth restriction, craniofacial abnormalities, and hypoplastic distal phalanges and nails.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn’s facial and digital findings are linked to maternal antiseizure therapy.

gaps.concept: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, disrupting embryonic DNA synthesis and causing craniofacial and limb malformations.
gaps.why_tested: A first-trimester medication exposure is paired with congenital anomalies.

gaps.concept: Thalidomide causes severe limb reduction defects, classically phocomelia.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn has markedly shortened limbs after maternal drug exposure.

gaps.concept: Tetracyclines cause fetal tooth discoloration and impaired bone growth.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnancy antibiotic exposure is linked to discolored primary teeth.

gaps.concept: Aminoglycoside exposure can cause fetal ototoxicity and congenital hearing loss.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn has sensorineural hearing loss after maternal antibiotic exposure.

gaps.concept: Prenatal diethylstilbestrol exposure is associated with clear cell vaginal adenocarcinoma and a T-shaped uterus in daughters.
gaps.why_tested: A young woman develops a rare vaginal cancer or uterine anomaly after historical maternal treatment.

gaps.concept: Fetal alcohol syndrome features growth restriction, microcephaly, short palpebral fissures, a smooth philtrum, and a thin upper lip.
gaps.why_tested: A child’s facial findings and developmental impairment are linked to prenatal exposure.

gaps.concept: Cocaine causes uteroplacental vasoconstriction, increasing placental abruption and fetal growth restriction.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with stimulant use develops painful third-trimester bleeding.

gaps.concept: Methimazole exposure early in pregnancy is associated with aplasia cutis; propylthiouracil is preferred during the first trimester.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn has a scalp skin defect after maternal hyperthyroidism treatment.

gaps.concept: Misoprostol exposure after an unsuccessful abortion attempt can cause Möbius sequence and limb defects.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn has facial paralysis with an exposure history.

gaps.concept: Mycophenolate exposure can cause microtia and cleft lip or palate.
gaps.why_tested: A transplant recipient’s fetus has distinctive ear and facial malformations.

gaps.concept: Late-pregnancy NSAID exposure can constrict the fetal ductus arteriosus; exposure after midpregnancy can reduce fetal renal function and amniotic fluid.
gaps.why_tested: Maternal analgesic use precedes oligohydramnios or premature ductal closure.

gaps.concept: First-trimester topiramate exposure increases the risk of cleft lip or palate.
gaps.why_tested: A patient taking an antiseizure drug has a fetus with an oral cleft.

gaps.concept: Poorly controlled maternal diabetes during organogenesis increases congenital malformations, especially caudal regression syndrome and cardiac defects.
gaps.why_tested: A fetus has sacral agenesis in a pregnancy complicated by pregestational diabetes.
